I have been bringing my dogs to Ambassador Animal Clinic for years, and I truly cannot say enough wonderful things about this clinic and the people who work there.

The staff has always been incredibly kind, compassionate, and caring, but Judy, one of their veterinary technicians, holds a very special place in my heart. She is absolutely phenomenal and one of the kindest people I have ever met. She is gentle, patient, caring, and incredibly attentive with my dogs. She takes the time to make them feel comfortable and treats them with so much genuine compassion.

One of my babies passed away in my arms at the clinic, and that is something I will never forget. It was pouring rain that day, and the veterinarian was incredibly patient and waited after closing for my partner and my dog’s best friend to arrive so my baby could be surrounded by the people and companion who loved him. It obviously wasn’t an ideal situation, but the compassion and understanding they showed us by allowing us that extra time so my baby could rest peacefully meant the absolute world to me.

That experience showed me that this isn’t just a place where animals receive medical care. These are people who understand that our pets are our family and that sometimes the most important thing they can give us is kindness, patience, and dignity during an incredibly painful moment.

My two dogs now have been patients there for the past couple of years, and Judy continues to be absolutely wonderful with them. Even though Ambassador Animal Clinic is out of our way, we still choose to make the drive because I trust this clinic and the people there completely.

Judy is truly one of a kind, and I am so grateful for the care she has given my babies over the years. If you are looking for a veterinary clinic where your pets will be treated with genuine compassion and where the people truly care, I cannot recommend Ambassador Animal Clinic enough.

This was from a couple of years ago, I was so enraged I think I blocked it out until now.  I had an appointment for 10 AM Saturday, where we discussed a pretty serious dental procedure for my dog.  He also got some vaccines, one of which was a two dose.  There was a follow up appointment for three weeks later, again Saturday at 10, where he was going to get his second dose and we were to discuss the dental procedure further.  I left with an appointment card, that in hand written writing said "Appointment, Saturday, 10:00 AM."

So THREE weeks later, after much anticipation I show up, concerned about my dog's dental situation.  The girl at the front desk says "We don't take walk ins."  I said "I have an appointment."  She said, "you're not in our system, we don't take walk ins."  So, I go out to my car, get the appointment card (that she personally wrote) come back in show it to her to which she replies "Is this for a vaccine?"  I said "Yes, he is getting a vaccine, but were also going to discuss his dental procedure."  She said "Well this is for a vaccine only and we don't take walk-ins."

Ok, I AM NOT A WALK-IN!  I didn't just WALK-IN.  At this point at the very least don't treat me like some bum off the street.  All I had was a quick question for the doctor and I would have scheduled the procedure.  You would think that after handing her a hand written note that she personally wrote that said APPOINTMENT, 10:00 AM, she would have been able to find a minute for the doctor to talk to me, but it was still "We don't take walk-ins."

I was so livid about the matter, I never went back and had anxiety about going to another vet for a while.  He never got the procedure, he is still alive, but his teeth are a MAJOR problem.  I really wish they honored their "appointment."  I do partly blame myself, but I have temper problem and didn't want to end up in jail over be called a walk-in.

On top of that, they attempted to take my kitten to the back without me present because the doctor “scheduled something else,” despite the fact that I had an appointment and nothing was communicated beforehand. My appointment was at 2:00 pm it’s now almost 3:30 pm and nothing has been done. All she needed is a single shot.

Horrible Experience - My Cat Is Worse Off After Surgery

I took my cat to this clinic with a simple concern—a bump on her rear end with some discharge. Instead of mainly addressing that, I was told she needed immediate surgery for pyometra (removal of the uterus), something I had never heard of. I was completely shocked because she seemed fine besides the bump, but the doctor told me that without the surgery, she could die within hours or days. I felt completely pressured into going through with the surgery, even though my cat is elderly (16 years old) and I don’t have a lot of money and I repeatedly expressed that, but was told there was just no other way.
In the end, I drained my savings and opened multiple credit cards to pay for the $2,500 surgery, hoping it would help my cat. But instead of getting better, she developed severe digestive issues. She lost so much weight that I could feel every bone in her body, she stopped eating, became severely constipated, and vomited after almost every meal.
I booked a follow-up appointment to express my concerns, but the doctor seemed indifferent. I was told that the surgery was necessary and that I had missed a three-day follow-up appointment—something no one reminded me about, not the doctor nor the front desk and was told by the doctor that it wasn’t their responsibility to reach out to me in any way, mind you the only reminder was on a piece of paper with a list of medication instructions in small lettering in the bottom of the paper. I was made to feel like I was in the wrong, despite being the one who just spent everything I had on my cat’s care.
Now, my cat’s condition has worsened to the point where she has organ issues, and they want me to pay an additional $1,600 for more treatment on top of the $2,500 I already paid. This clinic does not seem to care about your pet’s well-being; they just want your money. I am now over $5,000 in debt, and my cat is worse off than before.
Please, before bringing your pet here, consider other options that will actually help your animals health and won't leave you financially ruined.
